summary: An open-source, vendor-neutral standard for runtime governance of AI agents. Defines how development, compliance, and security teams can establish granular policies governing agent behavior: what agents may do, must not do, when humans must approve, and what must be logged.

risk_tiers.description: Agent actions that are pre-approved and can execute without additional controls or human intervention.
criteria: Action is within explicitly permitted scope

risk_tiers.description: Agent actions that may proceed but must be logged with full evidence trail for audit and review purposes.
Agent actions that require explicit human approval before execution due to their consequential or irreversible nature.
criteria: Action affects user permissions or access
Action involves sensitive or personal data

risk_tiers.description: Actions that an agent must never perform regardless of context, forming hard safety boundaries.
criteria: Action violates legal or regulatory requirements
Action attempts privilege escalation beyond defined scope

key_obligations.obligation: Define explicit permission policies specifying allowed, denied, and human-approval-required actions for each agent using declarative policy files
Implement runtime policy enforcement that validates every agent action against defined policies before execution proceeds
Maintain comprehensive evidence logs capturing agent reasoning, actions taken, policy evaluations, and human approvals for complete auditability
Implement human-in-the-loop checkpoints at policy-defined intervention points with timeout and escalation procedures
Ensure policy portability across agent frameworks and runtimes using the vendor-neutral ACS specification format

enforcement_timeline: Open-source specification released June 2, 2026 at Microsoft Build. Framework-agnostic, works with any agent runtime. Supported in Microsoft Foundry and Azure AI.
recent_changes: Initial open-source release at Microsoft Build 2026 (June 2, 2026)
Integrated with Microsoft Foundry agent platform
Companion tools: Agent Eval for testing, MXC execution containers for isolation
